verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'off the coast of San Diego, California'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: timestamps throughout 'April 10, 2026'; R2: 'Friday, April 10'; R3: 'April 10'; R4: 'April 10'; R5: 'April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm the date as Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely match the time and time zones for splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'historic 10-day trip to the moon'; R3: '10-day mission'; R4: 'record-breaking 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe it as a 10-day mission around the Moon, despite precise duration being 9 days +1 hour; common approximation supported.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman... Christina Koch and Victor Glover... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and... Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and... Jeremy Hansen'; R4: 'Koch, Glover, Hansen and Wiseman'
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exactly these four crew members.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is expected to begin its reentry into Earth's atmosphere just before the Artemis II splashdown time.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: reentry blackout '7:53 p.m. ET', splashdown '8:07 p.m. ET'; R2: blackout '7:53 p.m.', splashdown '8:07 p.m.'; R3: entry '7:53 p.m.', splashdown '8:07 p.m.'; R4: entry interface '7:53 p.m. ET', splashdown '8:07 p.m.'
verifications.reasoning: Reentry (entry interface) begins ~14 minutes before splashdown at 8:07 p.m., directly matching 'just before'.

verifications.claim: NASA provides live coverage of the Orion capsule reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Watch live return coverage on NASA+...'; R3: 'Watch live return coverage on NASA+...'; R4: 'NASA's livestream'; R5: 'NASA will livestream the event on its various platforms'
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources explicitly mention live coverage of reentry and return.

verifications.claim: Major news outlets provide live coverage of the Orion capsule reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: CBS News live updates; R4: NBC News live blog; R5: USA TODAY Network livestream and live coverage
verifications.reasoning: CBS, NBC, and USA TODAY (major outlets) provide live coverage of splashdown/reentry.
